scenario: A logistics analytics dashboard keeps records only for truck trips longer than 300 km because shorter trips are processed through a local-dispatch module. The transport planner wants the average trip distance across all trips.

data.description: Only trip distances above 300 km are observed. Distances are modeled as Normal with known standard deviation sigma = 120 km.

question: Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean trip distance mu across all truck trips, and (b) the fraction of trips that appear in the analytics dashboard.
naive_answer: The average truck trip is about 356 km because that is the dashboard mean.
naive_trap: The dashboard excludes all short-haul trips, so the observed mean is an upper-tail mean rather than the fleet-wide mean.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: Solve 356.04 = mu + 120*lambda((300-mu)/120). Step 2: The solution has alpha about 1.3, so mu = 300 - 1.3*120 = 144. Step 3: The recorded fraction is sf(1.3) = 0.0968.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu):
    a=(300-mu)/120
    return mu + 120*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a) - 356.04
mu=brentq(eq,-500,299.99)
frac=norm.sf((300-mu)/120)
assert abs(mu-144) < 6 and abs(frac-0.0968) < 0.005
